mailboxes.aliasHint: An alias address accepts mail and forwards it to one or more mailboxes (comma-separated).
mailboxes.bannerImap: IMAP/SMTP mode ({{host}}:{{port}}, domain {{domain}}). IMAP cannot create mailboxes — create it on the mail server, enter the address and password here, and the platform will verify the credentials and link the mailbox.
mailboxes.bannerMailcow: Mailcow API mode (domain {{domain}}). Mailboxes are really created, archived and deleted on the mail server.
mailboxes.bannerNone: No mail server connected: mailboxes are only stored in the platform database and will not appear on the server. Set MAILCOW_API_URL + MAILCOW_API_KEY or IMAP_HOST.
mailboxes.confirmDeleteDesc: The mailbox and all its data will be irrevocably removed from the mail server. This is the second stage of the two-step deletion (after archiving).
mailboxes.createDesc: The address is optional — it is derived from the first and last name (Ivan Ivanov -> i.ivanov). An empty password means auto-generation.
mailboxes.createDescImap: The mailbox must already exist on the mail server. Enter its address and password — the platform will verify the credentials over IMAP and link the mailbox.
mailboxes.localPartPatternHint: How to build the address from the employee's first and last name. It must match your company's convention, otherwise the platform generates an address that does not exist on the server.
mailboxes.passwordRequiredPlaceholder: mailbox password on the mail server
mailboxes.pushFlags: Mark messages read on the server
mailboxes.reconcileClean: No differences — the platform and the mail server match.
mailboxes.reconcileHelp: Reconciliation compares platform mailboxes with the mail server in both directions. Review the report first — it changes nothing — and only then apply the chosen direction. It also looks for owners: when a mailbox address matches an employee email, applying links the mailbox to them and it shows up in their mail.
mailboxes.reconcileProbeNote: The server does not expose a mailbox list, so only mailboxes known to the platform were checked, via a live IMAP login. Mailboxes created on the server outside the platform cannot be seen in this mode.
mailboxes.reconcilePullHint: The mail server is the source of truth: missing mailboxes are imported into the platform and differing values are pulled from the server.
mailboxes.reconcilePushDisabled: The current mail server cannot create mailboxes through an API.
mailboxes.reconcilePushHint: The platform is the source of truth: missing mailboxes are created on the server and differing values are pushed there.
mailboxes.selfService: Let employees connect their own mailbox
mailboxes.selfServiceHint: The employee enters the mailbox address and password; the platform verifies them against the server
mailboxes.settingsHelp: Values from the environment (.env) apply until a field is changed here. Clear a field to fall back to the environment value. Active mode: {{mode}}.
mailboxes.subtitle: Manage mailboxes on the corporate domain. Deletion is two-step: archive first, then delete permanently.
mailboxes.testHelp: Checks the chain in order: settings -> port -> IMAP -> login -> folders -> SMTP, stopping at the first failure. Mailbox address and password are optional — without them only settings and port reachability are checked.
mailboxes.title: Corporate mailboxes

mailboxes.tunnelTlsHint: Usually unnecessary over an SSH tunnel — SSH already encrypts it
mailboxes.userIdHint: With a user set, the mailbox shows up in their Mail section: the platform creates a mail account for them.

errors.nameRequired: A stage needs a name — the name is what carries the meaning; the platform has no roles.
errors.approverRequired: At least one approver is required: the engine will not start a stage without them.
errors.predicateWithoutValue: A predicate in the condition has no value — pick one or remove the row.

editor.toggleError: Could not change the route state
editor.gapBody: An object with this value cannot be submitted for approval — add a branch or an “otherwise” stage. Whoever presses “submit” will see the refusal, so it is better to close the gap here.
editor.signatureNotLastTitle: The initiator's signature is not last
editor.signatureNotLastBody: An approval finishes when the last step is done — and there are further steps after the signature stage in this route. That turns the signature from a final act into an intermediate confirmation. If you did mean the author's signature, move the stage to the last step.
editor.stagesHint: Steps run top to bottom; stages inside one step are approved simultaneously. A refusal at any stage rejects the whole process at once. A conditional stage joins the approval only when its condition matched.
editor.noStages: There are no stages — the route cannot run, and no object can be submitted through it.
editor.fallbackHint: otherwise — when no condition in the step matched
editor.cannotDeleteLast: The last stage cannot be deleted — a route without stages cannot run
editor.deleteConfirmBody: Approvals already under way are not affected — they run on the route snapshot taken at start. Only what is submitted from now on changes.
editor.noApprovers: no approvers — the stage will not run
editor.stepHint: Stages with the same step number are approved simultaneously; different numbers run one after another.
editor.stageNameHint: The platform has no roles — the stage name is what carries its meaning.
editor.initiatorHint: Whoever submitted the object approves it — the actual person becomes known at start. Such a stage is placed last: it is the author's signature.
editor.requireDocumentHint: The stage can only be approved with a file attached. It does not affect a refusal: there is no document for the refuser to sign.
editor.approversHint: The list is replaced wholesale: exactly what is selected now is what gets saved.
editor.otherwiseHint: The stage runs only when no condition in its step matched. An “otherwise” stage cannot have a condition of its own.
